origins: Losing work, retiring, being laid off, being unable to work because of illness, or caring for children at home can bring a painful sense of having no value. Many of us were taught that productive people matter and the rest do not. Society often reinforces it by asking “what do you do?” and treating the answer as status.
teaches: Jesus said that two sparrows are sold for a penny, and not one falls to the ground apart from the Father’s will, and then He said we are worth more than many sparrows. God says we are precious and honored in His sight, and that He loves us. Paul says God proves His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. Our worth was set by Him before we earned anything, and it cannot be reduced by unemployment.
self_statements: I contribute nothing without a paycheck.
I am a drain on everyone.
Everyone else is doing something and I am not.
I have no purpose without a job.
People do not respect someone who is not working.
errors: Feeling useless and concluding that I am worthless.
Believing that I am either employed and valuable or unemployed and worthless.
Calling myself “unemployed” as if it were a character trait.
Dismissing everything I give to others because it is unpaid.
questions: Who loved me before I held any job, and why?
What do I give to people that is not paid?
If a friend lost a job, would I say they were worthless?
What does God say about my worth during this season?
What do I do each day that matters, even if small?
Who needs me, and for what?
truth: My worth was settled by God’s love before I worked and will remain when I am not working. A job is a place to serve and provide, but it is not what makes me valuable. In a season without work I can still be loved, still be useful, and still be who God made me.
hw_truths: I am worth more than many sparrows.
God’s love does not depend on my paycheck.
I am valuable in every season.
I give in ways no payroll counts.
A job loss is a loss, not a verdict.
I can serve and be loved without earning it.
log: Each day, write one thing you gave or did for someone that has nothing to do with pay.
actions: Write Matthew 10:31 on a card and carry it.
Write down ways you help family, friends, church, or neighbors.
Tell a trusted person how you feel.
Share the heaviness of this season with someone who can listen.
Reach out to one person or resource about work options this week.
prayer: Father, You love me apart from anything I produce. When I feel worthless without a job, remind me that You value me. Guide my next step and let me rest in Your love today. Amen.
hw_questions: Who loved me before I had a job?
What do I give that is not paid?
What would I say to a friend in my place?
What does God say about my worth?
What is one small thing I can do today?
Who can I talk with about how I feel?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I am worth more than many sparrows, with or without a job.”
